-122.25620,37.85600.name: Alta Bates In Vitro Fertilization Program
-122.25620,37.85600.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-90.59626,44.56041.name: Genesis Midwest, LLC
-90.59626,44.56041.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-1.47091,53.80661.name: Care Fertility Leeds
-1.47091,53.80661.state: Seacroft Hospital, York Road, Leeds, LS14 6UH, United Kingdom
-1.47091,53.80661.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-57.63438,-25.28005.name: Neolife Medicina y CirugÃ­a Reproductiva
-57.63438,-25.28005.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. Website: http://neolife.com.py/. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere. No street address resolved, so this point is the city or the country rather than the centre.

4.91300,52.35600.name: Corbion
4.91300,52.35600.desc: A Dutch company fermenting engineered algae and microbes into food ingredients, lactic acid and omega-3 oils. Products of fermentation are generally not labelled as engineered even when an engineered organism made them, because the organism is not in the final product — so this is a substantial route by which genetic engineering enters food while remaining outside every labelling debate.

-77.02270,38.89440.name: EPA — biopesticide and plant-incorporated protectant registrations
-77.02270,38.89440.desc: The US register of pesticidal substances produced by plants themselves, including Bt traits. A plant that makes its own insecticide is registered as a pesticide, which puts the insecticide in the seed rather than in a tank and outside every measure of pesticide application.

-77.02270,38.89440.name: Anastasia / RNAi biopesticide sector
-77.02270,38.89440.desc: Sprayed double-stranded RNA silences a gene in a target pest, with no organism modified. Nothing living is altered so no biosafety framework applies, and the mechanism is sequence-specific so pesticide assumptions about dose and residue do not fit. Both categories were built for something else.

-118.39700,34.06300.name: Baum Hedlund and the glyphosate plaintiffs’ bar
-118.39700,34.06300.desc: The plaintiffs’ firms that brought the glyphosate cases and won the first verdicts. Litigation of this kind is the only mechanism that has extracted money from this industry at scale, and it runs on contingency fees rather than on any regulator’s finding.
